# HOW TO ADD A DASHBOARD
# 1. Copy this file in the same folder and give it a short name, e.g. tick-research.qmd
#    (files that start with "_" are ignored, so this template never appears on the site).
# 2. Fill in the title, description, date and categories below.
# 3. Keep ONE of the three options and delete the other two.
# 4. Save. The Dashboards page lists it automatically.
title: "Dashboard title"
description: "One sentence about what people can explore."
date: "2026-11-01"
categories: [Tableau]
---

Short introduction: what the data is, where it comes from, what to look at first.

<!-- OPTION A: Tableau Public
     In Tableau Public, click Share, copy the link, and paste it below
     after src= (add ?:showVizHome=no&:embed=true at the end). -->
```{=html}
<div class="embed-frame">
  <iframe src="https://public.tableau.com/views/YOUR_WORKBOOK/YOUR_SHEET?:showVizHome=no&:embed=true"
          title="Dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>
</div>
```

<!-- OPTION B: Dash or Streamlit app hosted elsewhere
     (Render, Hugging Face Spaces, Streamlit Community Cloud). Paste its address. -->
```{=html}
<div class="embed-frame">
  <iframe src="https://your-app.onrender.com" title="Dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>
</div>
```

<!-- OPTION C: An interactive Plotly chart saved as HTML
     In Python:  fig.write_html("dashboards/files/my-chart.html", include_plotlyjs="cdn")
     Put the file in dashboards/files/ and point to it below. -->
```{=html}
<div class="embed-frame">
  <iframe src="files/my-chart.html" title="Chart" loading="lazy"></iframe>
</div>
```
